findings.title: Dome shell has no collider and is not an occluder: Pip walks inside the dome and disappears completely behind it
findings.problem: The dome is two half-hemisphere meshes (inner starfield BackSide R=2.55, outer cream shell R+.06) at (-6.1, .15, -5.3). The only collider is a 1.2×2×1.2 box around the telescope pier (room.ts:69). The shell, the 2.85 m platform ring and the navy disc have no colliders, so Pip can walk straight through the cream shell into the dome. I walked Pip to (-5.34,-6.74), behind the telescope and inside the shell. From the front orbit Pip stands inside the sky (shot 66). After a 180° orbit, the opaque cream shell hides 100% of Pip at the game camera (shot 72) and at zoom 9 (shot 66b). The shell is about 2.6 m tall and is not in the occluder set (only pillars fade, decor.ts:55), so it never fades. The same shell takes up the left 40% of the frame next to the rack in shot 33. This is the 'camera hides Pip' failure that AGENTS 8 and DR-12 forbid. Walking through a solid-looking cream wall also breaks the physical read of the room: the player can't tell the dome from a painted backdrop.
findings.fix: In dressObservatory (room.ts:68-73), add a ring of thin solid() boxes along the back half-circle of the shell: 12 segments of 0.15×2.6×1.4 m at radius 2.6 around (dx,dz) for angles π..2π, each rotated tangentially. Add a low solid disc (cylinder collider r=2.85, h=.16) for the platform so props and Pip stand on it rather than in it. Register shellOut (and the starfield dome) as camera occluders using the same mechanism the pillars use (decor.ts:55 / game.ts occluder list), so they fade to ≤0.25 opacity when they sit between the camera and Pip. Use alpha-hash/dither, per DR-78, so the outline doesn't ghost. Alternatively, cut the shell to a quarter-sphere 'apse' that is lower at the room-facing sides.
findings.verify: Re-run mockups/review5/tools/observatory-models/11-recheck.mjs. walk(-5.4,-7.0) must stop outside the shell (player.z > -2.5 or the path is blocked). From the 180° orbit (shot 72), Pip must be visible with at least 70% of its pixels, or the shell must be faded. Re-run g.audit(.02) to confirm zero new overlaps.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced both halves. room.ts:69 has only a 1.2×2×1.2 pier collider, and the shell (room.ts:72) isn't in game.occluders (only pillars/interior walls, decor.ts:47-55, game.ts:387-388). Pip walked in through the open front to (-7.23,-6.23), then out through the cream shell sideways to (-3.29,-6.75), then back in through it to (-5.13,-6.97); every walk arrived. After a 180° orbit, the opaque shell hides Pip completely at both the default zoom and zoom 9. A player doesn't need to clip through anything for this: entering the dome through its intended open front and orbiting is enough.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-observatory-models-02-inside-dome-front-cam.jpg (Pip inside via the open front, visible)
mockups/review5/shots/verify-observatory-models-03-inside-dome-orbit180.jpg (same Pip fully hidden by the shell)
mockups/review5/tools/verify-observatory-models/01-room.mjs output: 'out through shell true {x:-3.29,z:-6.75}', 'back in through shell true {x:-5.13,z:-6.97}'
findings.fix_correction: Collider: don't use 2.6 m-tall boxes at r 2.6. The shell is a hemisphere, so above ~0.5 m those boxes would sit outside the visible curve and thrown props would hit invisible walls. Use ~12 segments about 1.2 m tall (y 0–1.2) centred at r≈2.45, just inside the base of the shell, on the back half only (angles π..2π). Occlusion: decorRoot parts are batched, so the shell and the BackSide starfield dome need their own cloned transparent materials on game.root, pushed into game.occluders, as decor.ts:47-48 does for interior walls. The fade uses a single ray (game.ts:387), so a broad 5 m shell also needs a chest/head ray, or the DR-12 three-point check.

findings.title: Gallery light rail and its 7 lamps float in mid-air when the back wall cuts away
findings.problem: The brass light rail (box 9×.06×.1 at y 3.2, z -D+.4 = -7.6) is parented to decorRoot `r`. Its seven 'hot' lamp cylinders are parented to game.root (room.ts:94). The panels, banner and safety note it lights are parented to kit.back, which cuts away whenever the camera orbits behind the back wall. The rail stays put, so once the camera passes behind the back wall a 9 m brass bar with seven glowing pucks hangs across the room at 3.2 m with nothing holding it up, and the exhibits it should light have gone. It's the most noticeable artefact in the room at the game camera (shots 64 and 72). Even with the wall present, the rail has no brackets to the wall or ceiling. It is 0.4 m out from the wall with nothing joining them (shot 20). This breaks DR-72 (nothing floats) and DR-75 (cutaway must not leave odd remnants).
findings.fix: In room.ts:94, parent the rail and its lamp cylinders to kit.back instead of r/game.root. Convert the positions to kit.back's local frame: rail at (x0+3*step, 3.2, .4), lamps at (x0+i*step, 3.12, .45), so the rail cuts away with the wall. Add 3 wall brackets: box(.05,.05,.4) at x = x0, x0+3*step and x0+6*step, from z .15 to .4 at y 3.2. Point each lamp hood toward its panel (rotation.x ≈ .5) so the rail reads as a track light. Keep the two pointLamps on game.root.
findings.verify: Retake observatory-models-64-gallery-from-behind and -72: no brass bar may appear without the back wall. Retake 20-gallery-left: the brackets touch the wall face (z offset ≤1 cm).
findings.verify_reason: room.ts:94 puts the 9 m rail on decorRoot and the 7 hot lamp pucks on game.root, while the panels, header and note are on kit.back (room.ts:89-92). With the back wall cut away, the bar and pucks hang across the room at 3.2 m with no exhibits; in shot 64 the bar crosses right over Pip's head. There's no bracket in code; the rail sits ≈0.2 m in front of the wall face. This only shows when the player orbits behind the back wall and doesn't affect play or teaching, so it's polish (P2), not P1.

findings.title: No physical cable from the roof receiver rack to the bench: the receiver line ends in mid-air at the bench edge
findings.problem: The whole first transmission is about the receiver's cable picking up motor noise: 'roll the motor away, reroute the cable'. RX at (-3.25,-2.45) is 'where the receiver's cable leaves the rack'. Yet nothing in the room joins the rack, at (RX.x-.3, RX.z-.2) = (-3.55,-2.65) with its right face at x≈-3.1, to the bench, whose left end is at x≈-2.15. The two red TubeGeometry routes on the bench start at local x=-2.2, y=.02, at the bench's edge, and stop there (station.ts:127-130). In the room shots there is a visible 1 m gap of bare floor between the rack and the bench (shots 63, 63b, 60). In the bench view the red cable runs off the left edge of the bench into nothing (shot 43, crop 43c). The player can't see that the bench line is the rack's line, so moving the motor away 'from the receiver' and rerouting 'past the motor' have no physical anchor. In a game whose star is the cable (AGENTS 4), the only cable in the room is a short bench decal.
evidence: src/stations/observatory/station.ts:127-130 (cable splines start at x=-2.2 on the bench top)
findings.fix: In station.ts buildBench, extend both cable splines with a floor run. Start at the rack's front-right jack (world RX.x+.15, .35, RX.z+.12), drop to the floor at y .03, run along the floor to the bench's left leg (t.x-2.15, .03, t.z±.4), climb the bench end, and join the existing points. cableNear should pass within 0.3 m of the motor cart's start spot (-3.7,-1.1). cableClear should run behind the rack and the back of the bench. Add a jack box on the rack front: rbox(.12,.1,.06) INK, plus a brass cyl socket at (RX.x-.3+.3, .35, RX.z-.2+.37). Optionally clamp the floor run with 2–3 cable clips (box .06×.02×.08) so it reads as fixed, not grabbable.
findings.verify: Retake shots 63/63b: a continuous red lead from the rack's jack to the bench RECEIVER jack. Retake the bench view (43): the lead enters from the left edge of the bench and visibly continues toward the rack. tests/station-observatory.spec.ts still passes.
findings.verify_reason: Both TubeGeometry routes start at bench-local x=-2.2 (station.ts:129,131), i.e. at the bench's left edge (bench 4.3 m wide centred at x=0). The rack's right face is at x≈-3.1 (room.ts:81), so about 1 m of bare floor separates them. Shot 63 and my bench crop show the red lead running off the left edge of the bench into nothing. The reroute lever (PAST MOTOR / CLEAR OF MOTOR) therefore only moves a cable on the bench top, while the motor sits off the bench, so the physical cause the station teaches isn't visible.
findings.fix_correction: The cable points live in the bench `top` group's local frame (table at world (0,1,-2.45), station.ts:64,102). Convert the world floor-run points by subtracting (0,1,-2.45): floor y .03 becomes local y -.97, and the rack jack at world (RX.x+.15,.35,RX.z+.12) becomes local (-3.10,-.65,.12). Alternatively build the floor run as a separate tube on game.root in world coordinates. Keep it non-colliding decor so the cart can still roll over it.

findings.title: Job items don't use the job-yellow language, while yellow crates, beanbags and chairs do
findings.problem: The first job item, the motor cart, is teal '#5f8fa8' with a red drum (observatory.ts:7). Meanwhile decorative clutter uses the job yellow. The placed beanbag at (-6.8,3.2) has no colour, so it takes the prefab default '#ffc94d' (prefabs.ts:26). The chair at (1.6,1.6) is '#ffc94d' (observatory.ts:10). The clutter palette includes '#ffd66b' (observatory.ts:21), which produces about a dozen yellow star-chart crates and yellow beanbags. In the survey and start shots the brightest, most saturated yellow shapes are the crate stack behind the bench, the yellow beanbag on the spawn rug and the yellow chair. None of them is part of the job, and the cart blends in with the teal coworker and teal crates. This breaks DR-45 (job items share one visual language, and no decorative clutter uses it) and DR-43 (the goal should be among the top-contrast shapes).
findings.fix: In observatory.ts: drop '#ffd66b' from clutter.colors and replace it with a muted brass '#c9a46a' or the cream '#e9dcc0'. Give the placed beanbag at (-6.8,3.2) an explicit colour, e.g. '#6f6ab8', and change the chair at (1.6,1.6) to '#3f7fd6'. Give the motor cart the job language: tint its tray '#ffc629' with an ink hazard stripe (two box(.04,.092,.75) INK bands on the long sides of the tray in the 'cart' builder, prefabs.ts:109-115), or wrap the drum in a yellow band with ink stripes in buildMotor (station.ts:167). Then change the prefabs.ts:26 beanbag default away from '#ffc94d' so no level inherits job yellow by accident.
findings.verify: Retake the start and survey shots. List the props within 25 ΔE of #ffc94d in the frame: only the motor cart (and the bench/grab cue) may remain.
findings.verify_reason: In code, the motor cart is '#5f8fa8' teal (observatory.ts:7), the chair at (1.6,1.6) is '#ffc94d' (observatory.ts:10), the colour-less beanbag (observatory.ts:12) inherits the prefab default '#ffc94d' (prefabs.ts:26), and '#ffd66b' is in clutter.colors (observatory.ts:25), so the crates, beanbag, chair and mug recipes all produce job-yellow decoys (clutter.ts:34-49 pick(r,c)). My start shot shows several yellow crates, yellow beanbags and the yellow chair on the violet rug as the brightest shapes, while the job cart is muted teal. That fails DR-45's check.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-observatory-models-02-inside-dome-front-cam.jpg (yellow crates and yellow beanbags around the dome; the cart reads teal)

findings.title: Beanbags are round lumps in coworker hues: 13 of them read as lying blobs or dumplings
findings.problem: The room has 13 beanbags: 2 placed plus 11 from the 'lounge' and 'reading' recipes (scene count, 08-count.mjs). Their colours come from the clutter palette, and include '#8fd3c8' (an exact BLOBC coworker hue, kit.ts:10), '#9b7bf0' (near BLOBC '#b392f0') and the default '#ffc94d' (also in BLOBC). The model is a squashed sphere plus a back lobe sphere, a thin torus seam and a small dark dimple (prefabs.ts:130-136). At the game camera and top-down (shots 06, 70) they read as round pastel lumps the same size and colour as the blob astronomers standing next to them. At zoom 9 (shots 10-o90, 12-dome) the seam and dimple are lost under the toon ramp, so they look like dumplings or lying blobs, not pear-shaped sacks. The teal one by the dome in shot 12 sits beside the teal-scarfed coworker, and the two shapes are nearly the same. This is the known P5 'bread loaf' issue, repeated 13 times in this room.
findings.fix: Remodel beanbag in prefabs.ts:130-136 as a pear sack. Use a LatheGeometry profile: base radius .44 at y 0, belly .46 at y .18, waist .3 at y .45, top .22 at y .58. Tilt the top lobe 15° back, with a deep seat dent (sphere .24, scaled y .25, offset z +.1, colour −15% L). Add 4 vertical seam tubes (TubeGeometry r .012) from the base to the top, plus a small fabric tag (box .08×.05×.01, cream) at the front. Use a fabric palette that never overlaps BLOBC: corduroy brown '#8a5a3c', denim '#3d5a8a', mustard-olive '#a89a3a', terracotta '#b8573f'. In clutter.ts, have lounge/reading pick beanbag colours from that fabric set rather than the level's accent list. Give the beanbag a cylinder collider (r .45) instead of the .9 box (see the audit finding).
findings.verify: Zoom-9 close-up of the reading corner (rerun 02-closeups.mjs → 10-reading-corner*) and a top-down orbit (06): a first-time viewer names 'beanbag', not blob or bread. Colour check: no beanbag within 15 ΔE of any BLOBC hue.
findings.verify_reason: A scene traverse found 13 beanbags (13 instances of the .43/.018 seam torus) and 10 lamp shades. The model is a squashed sphere plus a lobe, a thin seam and a dimple (prefabs.ts:130-137), and its colours come from the level palette, which includes the exact BLOBC hue '#8fd3c8' (kit.ts:10) and the default '#ffc94d'. At the game camera they read as pastel lumps (shots 11/12). They don't really get confused with coworkers, which have big eyes, so this is model-detail polish (P2), not P1.
findings.fix_correction: The proposed fabric palette (corduroy brown, denim, mustard-olive, terracotta) is desaturated, and DR-51 says fabric (chairs, beanbags, sofas) is saturated. Use saturated hues at least 15 ΔE from every BLOBC entry instead, e.g. red '#d64a3a', cobalt '#2e5fc7', plum '#a8327a', forest '#2f8a4f'. The rest of the fix (lathe pear sack, seat dent, seams, round collider at game.ts:124) is fine.

findings.title: Win push-in leaves out the dome light-up payoff and crops Pip at the left edge
findings.problem: When the last transmission is decoded, lightUp() brightens the dome. It adds a glow sprite and an 8-intensity point light at (dx,1.8,dz) = (-6.1,1.8,-5.3) (room.ts:108-110). The win camera instead pushes in on the bench and the gallery. In shots 50 (0.25 s) and 51 (1.5 s) the dome isn't in the frame at all, so the room's one celebratory change is never seen. Pip is cut by the left frame edge: only the helmet, one arm and the torso show, inside x 0–270 of 1440, outside the centre 70%. The result card then covers the right half of the frame.
findings.fix: Either (a) aim the observatory's winFocus (game.ts:398 winFocus/station focus) between the bench and the dome, at about (-3.0,1.4,-3.4), with a 3/4 yaw from the front-left so the bench, the rack and the dome are in frame and Pip sits at 40–60% of the width; or (b) move the light-up so it shows in the bench framing: light the 7 gallery panels and lamps in sequence, and send a sprite 'beam' from the rack mast. Also nudge the camera 0.8 m to Pip's left so Pip isn't clipped. Keep the extra light within the DR-66 budget by reusing the existing dome pointLamp (raise its intensity) instead of adding a sixth.
findings.verify: Rerun 05-bench.mjs and retake 50/51. Pip's bounding box and the lit dome (or the lit gallery) both sit inside the centre 70% before the result card slides in.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it at the default zoom. The push-in uses winFocus = table+0.5 offset 2.2 m to the right, distance 7, pitch .5 (game.ts:373,398). The dome at x=-6.1 is about 6 m to the left and never in frame, so lightUp (room.ts:109) is invisible. Pip is cut by the left frame edge, well outside the centre 70%. This fails the DR-11 check directly. The framing is shared by every station, but the observatory loses its only payoff to it.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:373 (pushing: target=f+right*2.2, distance 7 for any station)

findings.title: Carrying the 'roll' cart lifts it to head height and tilts it across Pip's face; the motor drum detaches on a tilt
findings.problem: Step 1 says 'Roll the noisy motor cart away', and the prompt while holding says 'Keep rolling it away'. In fact E lifts the 1.2 m mail cart: snap() gives the cart centre at y 1.30 while Pip's origin is at y 0.77, so the tray spans about 0.98–1.62 m and the motor rides on top to about 2.0 m (11-recheck.mjs output). At zoom 9 the cart swings to a 35–45° tilt in front of Pip and covers Pip's face and helmet (shot 41). At the default camera it hides the motor (shot 70). After set-down it lands tilted on a chair, and the drum and fan blades stick into Pip's arm (shot 42). The motor group copies the cart's quaternion, but its offset is world-up (`motor.position.set(p.x,p.y+.33,p.z)`, station.ts:313), so whenever the cart tilts the drum drifts off the tray, out of the cart's local frame. This breaks DR-65 (carried items level in front of the chest, never over the head) and contradicts the verb on the card.
findings.fix: (1) station.ts:313: apply the offset in the cart's frame: `const off=new T.Vector3(0,.33,0).applyQuaternion(qv); motor.position.set(p.x+off.x,p.y+off.y,p.z+off.z)`. (2) Make the cart a push prop, not a lift, the same way the heavy bookshelf already prompts 'heavy: push it'. Either flag spec.id==='motor' as push-only in game.ts's grab/carry code, so the body stays on its wheels at y .33 and is dragged at the handle (handle at -w/2 in prefabs.ts:115), or give the cart mass ≥30 so it uses the push path. Keep the carry target level (rotation locked to yaw) if it must stay a lift.
findings.verify: Rerun 05-bench.mjs: in 40/41, the cart's y stays ≤0.4 (snap().items motor.pos.y) and the tray stays level. In 42 the drum sits on the tray. A test asserting the motor item's y < .5 while held would guard it.
findings.verify_reason: The cart's mass is 8 (prefabs.ts:16), below the heavy-push threshold of mass≥15 (game.ts:331), so E lifts it to p.y+.55. snap() gave a carried cart centre at y 1.30 and 1.39 while rolling, against Pip at y 0.77. game.ts:331 only zeroes angvel each frame, so collisions tilt the cart ~40° (shot 12). station.ts:313 adds the .33 offset in world-up while copying the body's quaternion, so the drum slides off the tray when the cart tilts. On set-down the cart toppled onto its end (y .58, shot 13) with the drum stuck to the side of the tray.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-observatory-models-13-setdown-zoom9.jpg (cart landed on its end, drum stuck to its face)
02-cart-win.mjs output: carry motor y 1.2996, rolling y 1.3886, setdown y 0.58
findings.fix_correction: The heavy path triggers at mass ≥ 15 (game.ts:331), not ≥ 30. Don't change the 'cart' prefab mass globally: carts are used in garage (id 'robot'), meeting ('mail-cart' job item), qfn, spectrum and arcade. Add a per-spec override instead (e.g. PropSpec mass or push:true for id 'motor') read in game.ts:331. The quaternion-applied offset in fix part (1) is correct.

findings.title: Motor reads as a red cable reel, not a noisy motor
findings.problem: buildMotor (station.ts:167-169) is a red cylinder of r .2 × .42 with two ink end discs of r .21 and four cream fan blades outside one end, on a grey plate. That is the reel silhouette the cable floors use (a coloured drum with dark flanges). At the game camera it reads as a cable reel on a trolley (shots 01, 13, 70). Only the tiny 'MOTOR' tag says otherwise. The blades spin in the open with no guard. There is no shaft, cooling fins, terminal box or mounting feet, and no power lead. Its noise is shown only by 3-particle blue sparks every 0.5–1.1 s (station.ts:316), which are hard to see. For a job item whose physics is the point (EMI from a brushed motor), it has too few distinguishing cues (DR-62 asks for 2–4), and it borders on a false affordance (DR-17).
findings.fix: In buildMotor: swap the red drum for a ribbed motor body: cyl(.19,.19,.36) DMETAL or red, plus 8 longitudinal fins box(.03,.36,.05) around it. Add end bells cyl(.17,.2,.06) at each end, a brass shaft cyl(.025,.025,.12,'x') with a pulley cyl(.06,.06,.04,'x') on the non-fan end, and a terminal box rbox(.12,.08,.1) on top with a short black lead tube curving down to the cart tray. Add two mounting feet box(.08,.04,.32) under the body. Put a wire guard over the fan: torus(.16,.01) ×2 plus 4 spokes. While running, add a visible noise cue: a jagged blue 'arc' sprite or 3 concentric ring decals that pulse outward from the drum every 0.3 s (opacity ≤.4), shrinking as cartDistance grows.
findings.verify: Zoom-9 close-up of the cart (rerun 02-closeups.mjs → 13-rack-motor*) and a first-look naming at the default camera: 'motor', not 'reel'.
findings.verify_reason: buildMotor (station.ts:166-169) is just a red cyl r.2 × .42 with two ink end discs, four cream blades and a 'MOTOR' tag. At the default and zoom-9 cameras it reads as a red spool with dark flanges on a trolley, the same silhouette as the cable reels. There's no guard, shaft, fins, terminal box or lead. The noise cue is a 3-particle spark every 0.5–1.1 s (station.ts:316). The model has few cues, but this is polish.

findings.title: Telescope tube pokes through the dome shell; no slit; fork arms don't touch the tube
findings.problem: The tube group sits at y .15+1.05+.52 = 1.72 with rotation.x = -.75 and a 1.9 m tube (room.ts:75-78). The top cap ends about 1.28 m up the axis, at world y ≈ 2.65 and z ≈ -6.07, which is ≈ 2.62 m from the dome centre (-6.1,.15,-5.3). Its radius is .23 and the dome radius is 2.55, so the brass cap and the end of the tube come out through the cream shell. This is visible in the start view (shot 01, the tube tip above the dome) and clearly from the side (shots 62b, 32-side). The code comment says 'aimed up through the slit', but the shell is a plain half-sphere with no slit. The fork arms are at x=±.3 and the tube radius is .2, so there is a 0.1 m air gap with no trunnion pins and the tube floats between the arms (shot 12, 66).
findings.fix: Cut a slit in both dome meshes: build each SphereGeometry as two pieces with a 0.5 m wide gap (thetaStart offsets) along the meridian the tube points at, and add a brass rim torus segment along both slit edges. Or shorten the tube to 1.5 m and set rotation.x = -.6 so its tip stays ≥.25 m inside R. Add trunnion pins cyl(.04,.04,.12,'x') BRASS at (±.24, 0, 0) in tube space, so the fork arms (move them to x=±.26) visibly hold the tube.
findings.verify: Retake 62b and 32-side: no part of the tube outside the shell except through a framed slit. Zoom-9 shot 12: the fork arms touch the pins.
findings.verify_reason: By geometry, the tube group sits at world y 1.72, z -5.2, with rot.x -.75. The cap at local y 1.22 lands at y≈2.61, z≈-6.03, 2.57 m from the dome centre; with its .23 radius it crosses the R+.06=2.61 outer shell. In my orbit-180 zoom-9 shot the brass cap shows on the outside of the cream shell, and in 62b the tip pokes out at the top. There is no slit in the SphereGeometry. The fork arms' inner faces are at ±.27 against a tube radius of .2, leaving a 7 cm gap with no trunnions.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-observatory-models-06-orbit180-zoom9.jpg (yellow brass cap protruding through the outer shell)

findings.title: Rack, dome exterior and scope cabinet have big blank faces and unfinished backs
findings.problem: The receiver rack is an rbox of .9×1.5×.7 in NIGHT with three front panels, a dial each and 9 LED dots (room.ts:81-85). Its sides (1.05 m² each) and back (1.35 m²) are plain navy with no vents, handles, screws, cable entry or mast clamp (shots 33, 61). The mast pole just stands on the brass top. The outer dome shell, about 20 m², is uniform cream with no panel seams, ribs or hatch (shots 66b, 72, 65b). Seen from the gallery side, the scope cabinet's back (body rbox 1.6×1.0, station.ts:148) is a plain cream slab (shot 62b). All of these break DR-62 (no flat single-colour face over 0.5 m² without trim) and DR-63 (finished backs, because the player orbits).
findings.fix: Rack: add side vent slots (6× box(.02,.04,.5) INK at x=±.455), 4 rack-ear strips box(.04,1.4,.02) BRASS at the front corners with screw dots, a rear panel line box(.8,.02,.02) at 3 heights, and a cable gland cyl(.05) on the back where the mast lead enters. Add a mast clamp torus around the pole at y 1.56 and a coax tube from the mast down the back into the gland. Dome: add 8 radial ribs (TorusGeometry arc segments, tube .03, BRASS or #d8c9a8) on the outer shell plus a circumferential seam at 60% height. Scope back: add a vent grille (5 box(.9,.02,.01) INK) and a brass badge.
findings.verify: Orbit 180° at zoom 9 around the rack (rerun 04-closeups.mjs → 33*) and the dome (11-recheck.mjs → 72). No plain face larger than 0.5 m² remains.
findings.verify_reason: room.ts:81-85 gives the rack only front panels, dials and LEDs. Its side reads as plain navy in shot 33. The outer shell (room.ts:72) is uniform cream in my orbit shots. The scope cabinet back (station.ts:150, rbox 1.6×1.0 cream) is a plain slab in 62b. Each of these faces is well over 0.5 m², so they fail DR-62/63.

findings.title: ROOF RECEIVER plaque floats above the rack as a one-sided plane
findings.problem: The plaque is a bare PlaneGeometry(.8,.2) with a flat (MeshBasic, FrontSide) texture at y 1.72, tilted -.3, at z RX.z+.16 (room.ts:86). The rack's brass top is at 1.55, so the sign's bottom edge (~1.62) hangs about 7 cm above it with no stand. It is a single plane with no housing, so it vanishes edge-on (shot 33) and from behind. It reads as a floating label, not a mounted sign. In the start view the bouncing objective marker sits right over it (shot 12: 'ROO…ER').
findings.fix: Mount it on the rack's front face below the top: an INK backing box(.84,.22,.03) in the rack group at (0,1.36,.36), with the plaque plane at z .376 (0.5 cm off). Or put it on a small brass stand on the rack top: two posts box(.03,.1,.03) plus the backing box. Never leave a bare plane.
findings.verify: Retake 33 (side) and 61 (top). The sign has visible thickness and touches its mount, and from behind the back face is ink.
findings.verify_reason: room.ts:86 is a bare PlaneGeometry(.8,.2) with a flat material at y 1.72, tilted -.3, while the rack's brass top is at 1.55. It has no backing or stand. In shot 33 (side) it has vanished edge-on, and in shot 12 the objective marker sits on it ('ROO…ER'). It fails DR-72/63.
findings.fix_correction: A minor tweak: at rack-local y 1.36 the backing (.22 tall) would overlap the top front panel (y 1.01–1.31) and touch the brass lid at 1.49. Use y≈1.40 with height .16, or mount it on the rack top with posts.

findings.title: Clutter fills the exhibit gallery: a desk pod against the RADIO panel, crates and lamps between the plinths; the safety note is hidden behind them
findings.problem: The clutter lanes (observatory.ts:21) protect only the dome and the spawn-to-bench routes, so the 'pod', 'crates' and 'reading' recipes are free to fill the gallery strip, z -7.5 to -5. The audit lists a desk at (0.49,-6.97) with a monitor at (0.66,-6.97), jammed against the back wall under the RADIO and MICROWAVE panels. Its desk top at .95 m sits over the left end of the safety note, which is at y .9 (shots 20, 51). Purple and teal crates and a lamp-and-beanbag pair stand between the exhibit plinths (shots 21, 22, 64b). The plinths are .9 m tall with exhibits up to ~1.45 m, so they sit directly in front of the safety note band (y .73–1.07), and the dish covers 'safe: UV' (shot 20). The gallery stops reading as a curated exhibit wall and becomes a storeroom, and the plinth silhouettes merge with the crates.
findings.fix: Add a lane to observatory.ts clutter.lanes: {points:[[-.2,-7.2],[9.6,-7.2]],r:1.3}, which keeps everything from z ≈ -5.9 to the wall clear between x 0 and 9.6. Move the safety note to y 2.95 below the header, or split it into three short plaques on the UV/X-RAY/GAMMA panel frames (y 1.05, inside the frames). That also addresses the DR-49 wall-sentence rule.
findings.verify: Rerun 01-overview.mjs: g.audit lists no desk/monitor with z < -6. Retake 20-gallery-left and 64b: the floor in front of the 7 panels is clear except for the 3 plinths, and the safety text isn't covered.
findings.verify_reason: The clutter lanes (observatory.ts:26) don't cover the gallery strip. Shot 20 shows a desk and monitor jammed under the RADIO/MICROWAVE panels, purple crates between the plinths, and the dish covering 'is safe' in the safety note. Shots 21/22 also show two floor lamps interpenetrating near the lead box. One detail is wrong: the desk does not sit over the safety note. The note is 5.6 m wide centred at x0+3*step=4.24 (room.ts:92), so it spans x 1.44–7.04, and the desk at x≈.49 ends left of it.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/observatory-models-21-gallery-right.jpg (two lamps clipped into each other at right)
findings.fix_correction: The note can't move to y 2.95: the header plaque already occupies y 2.95 (room.ts:91, spanning y 2.74–3.16 above the panel brass bars at 2.74). Instead split the note into per-panel plaques inside the frames, or move the plinths to z ≈ -5.6 and lower the note to y .55 so the plinths no longer block it. The lane suggestion is fine.

findings.title: Laid-flat 1.5 m whip pushes into the scope cabinet; the route lever covers the '1.5 m' rack label
findings.problem: (a) The antenna mount is at bench-local (-1.12,.04,-.3). Laying the whip flat rotates it z = -π/2, so it points toward +x, and the r150 rod is drawn .1+1.5×.34 = .61 m long (station.ts:56, :235). Its tip lands at x ≈ -.51, inside the scope plinth and housing, which span x -.68..+.92 at z ≈ -.33. In shot 47a the flat rod runs across the scope's left frame and over the SIGNAL button. (b) The route lever base, rbox .26×.16 at (-1.22,.36) (station.ts:132-134), sits on top of the '1.5 m' rod caption (rack x -1.72+.289, z .1+.14). Its red knob covers the label in the default bench view (shots 43, 43c: '1.5 r'). R3A N9 asked for the captions to be readable. They now sit in front of the rods, but this one is covered by the lever instead, a partial regression.
findings.fix: (a) Lay the whip toward -x, away from the scope: `this.whip.rotation.z=this.vertical?0:Math.PI/2` (it then reaches x ≈ -1.73 over the rod rack, which is lower). Or lay it along z toward the back edge: rotation.x = -π/2. Add a small brass hinge cyl at the mount so the flat pose reads as folded. (b) Move the lever to (-1.25,.04,.52) and the ROUTE sign to (-1.62,.045,.58), or shift the rod captions to z .02 in front of the rack edge.
findings.verify: Rerun 05-bench.mjs. In 47a the flat r150 rod doesn't overlap the scope housing pixels. In 43c all four captions (3.1 cm, 17 cm, 75 cm, 1.5 m) are fully readable.
findings.verify_reason: (a) The mount is at bench-local x -1.12, and the whip is flattened with rotation.z=-π/2, pointing +x (station.ts:235). r150's rodLen is .61 (station.ts:56), so the tip reaches x≈-.51 at z -.3, y .16. The scope plinth spans x -.74..+.98 and the tilted body's front-bottom sits at z≈-.3, so the rod enters the scope base; my crop shows it running onto the scope frame. (b) Before rerouting, the route lever knob (station.ts:132, rotation.z +.5) covers the '1.5 m' caption ('1.5 r' in 43c). After rerouting the caption reads fully.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/observatory-models-46a-crop-whip-flat.jpg ('1.5 m' readable once the lever is flipped)

findings.title: Exhibit models read wrong: the dish is a salad bowl, the prism a grey can with a floating rainbow flag
findings.problem: Dish plinth (3.2,-6.3): a spherical cap of r .34 flipped to rotation.x 0.8π on a thin rod (room.ts:98). It has no feed horn, support arms or back rib, so from the front it reads as a white bowl (shots 20, 22). Prism plinth (6.2,-6.3): a 3-segment translucent cylinder (opacity .6) that shows as a grey can. Six coloured strips of .4 m stick straight out sideways into the air (room.ts:99-100), so the rainbow reads as a little flag. There is no white beam going in and no fan coming out. The lead box with its trefoil plaque reads fine. These exhibits illustrate the spectrum teaching, so their silhouettes matter.
findings.fix: Dish: tilt the cap 35° up and toward the room (rotation.x = -Math.PI*.3). Add a feed horn: 3 struts cyl(.012,.012,.38) from the rim to a focal cone cyl(.03,.05,.08) at .3 m in front. Add a yoke box(.06,.3,.06) ×2 and a back rib ring torus(.2,.015). Prism: use a proper triangular ExtrudeGeometry of side .3, depth .3, opacity .75 with an outline. Add an incoming white beam (box .5×.02×.02, MeshBasic white, opacity .6) from the left, and fan the 6 colour strips from the exit face as thin wedges (ShapeGeometry fan) lying 1 cm above the plinth top, not floating.
findings.verify: Zoom-9 retakes of 22-plinths and 20-gallery-left. First-look naming: 'radio dish' and 'prism splitting light'.
findings.verify_reason: The dish is a white spherical cap on a rod (room.ts:98) and reads as a bowl in shot 20. The prism block is grey and translucent, and its six strips stick out sideways as a little floating flag (shots 21, 22). There is no incoming beam.
findings.fix_correction: The prism is already a triangular prism: cyl(.2,.2,.3,3) has 3 radial segments (room.ts:99), so switching to ExtrudeGeometry adds nothing. The fix is orientation (stand a triangle face toward the camera), higher opacity with an outline, the incoming white beam, and a rainbow fan resting on the plinth top.

findings.title: Dome platform has no collider: pushed props and the astronomer sink into the 15 cm ring and disc
findings.problem: The platform ring is cyl(R+.25,R+.3,.14) with its top at y .14, and the navy disc is at y .15 (room.ts:69). Neither has a collider. The clutter lane keeps clutter off at load, but anything Pip pushes onto the platform rests at floor level, 14–15 cm down into it. In shot 12-dome-o70, after Pip walks up, the yellow and purple beanbags sit sunk into the lavender ring and onto the disc. The astronomer coworker at (-4.4,-4.4) stands ≈1.9 m from the dome centre, on the disc, with its body origin at floor level, so its base is buried 15 cm (observatory.ts:16, shots 32/60). g.audit can't see any of this because the platform isn't a collider.
findings.fix: Add a fixed cylinder collider (r 2.85, half-height .075, centre y .075) at (dx,dz), using the solid() pattern with RAPIER ColliderDesc.cylinder, so the platform is a real step (Pip's controller climbs .15 m). Lift the astronomer by setting the NpcSpot y offset to .15 if NpcSpot supports y, or move it to (-3.6,-3.2), off the disc.
findings.verify: Push a beanbag onto the platform (walk through it) and retake 12-dome-o70: the beanbag's bottom sits on the disc at y .15. Retake 60: the coworker's base is fully visible on the disc.
findings.verify_reason: The ring and disc (room.ts:69) have no collider. In shot 12-dome-o70 the purple and yellow beanbags sit sunk into the lavender ring and disc. The astronomer at (-4.4,-4.4) is 1.92 m from the dome centre, so it stands on the disc at floor level. The same is true of Pip: inside the dome at (-7.23,-6.23) the player stayed at y 0.770, the same as on the open floor, so Pip's boots are 15 cm into the disc. Autostep is .25 (game.ts:83), so a 0.16 m platform collider would be climbable.

findings.title: Ten identical floor lamps and the paired beanbag repeat across the room (copy-paste look); lamp bases read as black holes
findings.problem: The recipe list repeats 'reading' twice and also has 'lounge' (observatory.ts:21), so 37.5% of cluster draws produce a beanbag, and every 'reading' cluster is the same lamp + beanbag + paper. The scene has 10 identical lamps (cyl .18/.32 shade ×10) and 13 beanbags (08-count.mjs). The ivory cone shade, wood pole and large ink base disc (r .3, prefabs.ts:157-159) repeat in the same pose all over the survey (shot 02). The lamps are unlit (no bulb, no glow, known F15), and their dark .6 m base discs look like holes in the honey floor at the game camera (shots 01, 70). R5 research counted about 7 lamps; this build has 10, which is worse.
findings.fix: In observatory.ts:21, replace the second 'reading' with a room-themed recipe. Add 'atlas' to clutter.ts: a low table rbox(.9,.45,.6) with an open star-atlas decal, a globe sphere(.15) on a brass stand, a stool and a mug. Give the lamp prefab variants: shade colour from the accent list, height 1.3/1.5/1.7 (scale.y on the pole) and a tilt of ±8°. Shrink the base to cyl(.17,.2,.05) in DMETAL instead of INK, and add a warm emissive bulb sphere(.05) hot('#ffe7b0',1.2) inside the shade, with no extra point lights.
findings.verify: Recount with 08-count.mjs: lamps ≤5, no recipe >25% of clusters. Retake the survey: no two lamps identical in colour and height within 6 m.
findings.verify_reason: A scene traverse counts 10 identical lamp shades and 13 beanbags. The recipes list has 'reading' twice plus 'lounge', so beanbag recipes are 3/8 = 37.5% (observatory.ts:25; clutter.ts:38,44). Each lamp has an INK base disc of r .3 (prefabs.ts:158), which reads as a dark spot on the floor. DR-67 already lists the repeated observatory lamps as a known issue.

findings.title: Bookshelves are tinted the room's accent purple and filled with uniform, fully saturated candy-block books
findings.problem: The bookshelf board colour comes from the level's clutter colours ('#4a4380', '#9b7bf0' and so on, observatory.ts:21; shelf recipe clutter.ts:42 → color:pick(r,c)), so shelves are violet. Every book is the same box(.14,.34,d*.7) in saturated primaries (prefabs.ts:123-125), so the shelves read as rows of red, blue, green and yellow candy blocks, not star atlases (shots 31, 30, 02). That breaks DR-51: books are desaturated, and a level may tint accents but never the family. They are also the most saturated objects in the room, which competes with the job items. The colour-wrap fix (books cycling correctly) still holds: no wrap artefact was seen.
findings.fix: In the shelf recipe, don't pass the level colour to bookshelf: use a fixed office-neutral board ('#b98552' WOOD or METAL). In prefabs.ts:123-125, draw books from a desaturated set (dusty blue '#6d7fa3', sage '#8aa58a', oxblood '#8c4a4a', ochre '#b89a5a', slate '#5d6475'). Vary height .26–.36 and width .1–.16, tip one book per shelf by 12°, and leave one gap. Add a thin spine band box(w,.03,.005) in cream on every third book.
findings.verify: Retake 31-desk-shelf-cart. Mean chroma of the book pixels must be below that of the rug and the motor cart.
findings.verify_reason: The shelf recipe passes pick(r,c) as the board colour (clutter.ts:42), so the boards come out in the level's violets. Books cycle through the saturated set ['#e5484d','#3f7fd6','#6cc58a','#ffc94d','#b392f0','#8fd3c8'] (prefabs.ts:52,125). Shots 64/72 show purple shelves with candy-coloured books. That breaks DR-51, which wants desaturated books and no tinting of the prop family.

findings.title: Start-time audit: beanbag box collider overlaps paper by 3 cm (round prop on a square collider)
findings.problem: g.audit(.02) at start returns one overlap: beanbag @-5.94,-1.48 with paper @-5.44,-1.03, depth .03. The beanbag's physics shape is the .9×.9×.6 box from prefabs.ts:26, so a rotated cluster puts its invisible corner (reach .64 m) under nearby litter. DR-70 asks for zero overlaps at start, and DR-71 asks for round colliders on round props. g.audit(.005) also lists four desk/monitor contacts of .01, which are benign (the monitor rests on the desk).
findings.fix: Give beanbags (and plant, bin, cone, lamp base) a cylinder collider. In the prop body factory, use ColliderDesc.cylinder(h/2, w/2) when kind is in a ROUND set. In clutter.ts:44, move the reading recipe's paper to dz .75.
findings.verify: Rerun 01-overview.mjs: audit02 returns [].
findings.verify_reason: The underlying cause is real. Every dynamic prop gets a cuboid collider (game.ts:124), and the beanbag's is a .9×.6×.9 box (prefabs.ts:26), which fails DR-71's round-collider rule. The audit number didn't reproduce, though: my g.audit(.02) at start returned [], and g.audit(.005) gave the same beanbag/paper pair at depth .02, not .03. The overlap sits right at the threshold, so whether DR-70's start check fails depends on settle timing.
extra_evidence: 01-room.mjs output: audit02 [] ; audit005 [{beanbag @-5.94,-1.48 / paper @-5.44,-1.03, depth .02}, {paper / floor, .02}]

findings.title: Shared toon material mutated to DoubleSide by the dish exhibit
findings.problem: toon() caches materials by colour (toon.ts:34-44). room.ts:98 does `(bowl.material as T.Material).side=T.DoubleSide` on toon('#dfe3ea'). That same material is used for the mast crossbars (room.ts:84), every bench whip rod and spare rod (station.ts:141,144) and the series wire link, so all of them silently become double-sided. That doubles their fill and changes how the outline pass and AO treat them. room.ts:72 does the same to toon('#e9dcc0') (FrontSide, harmless today). The pattern is fragile: one prop's tweak changes many others in the instanced batches.
findings.fix: Clone before mutating: `bowl.material=(bowl.material as T.Material).clone();(bowl.material as T.Material).side=T.DoubleSide;`. Or add a `side` field to ToonOptions and include it in the cache key in toon.ts:35.
findings.verify: In page.evaluate, traverse the scene and check that the whip rod meshes' material.side === FrontSide (0), and that only the dish uses DoubleSide.
findings.verify_reason: toon() caches by colour/emissive/map/opacity only (toon.ts:34-44), and room.ts:98 sets side=DoubleSide on the shared toon('#dfe3ea'). At runtime every mesh coloured #dfe3ea (mast crossbars room.ts:84, wire link station.ts:118, whip rod station.ts:141, spare rods station.ts:144, dish) shares one material with side=2 (DoubleSide).
extra_evidence: 01-room.mjs scene output: dfe3ea material sides [2] (one shared material, DoubleSide)

findings.title: Wood floor is a little too bright (median luma 186–197)
findings.problem: The plank floor uses TX.woodPlanks('#dcb07a') (room.ts:65). Floor crops of the start shot measure median luma 197 next to Pip and 186 in the open floor (186 with ?norim), above DR-54's 140–185 band. The floor competes with the cream walls (luma ≈208) and the cream bench and plinths. With ?norim the honey props (yellow crates, cream beanbags, ivory lamp shades) sit within about 10–20 luma of the floor.

notes.models: The observatory has a real identity: a night-sky dome with constellation lines over a brass-and-cream telescope, a navy receiver rack with a mast, a seven-panel spectrum gallery with lit hoods, and a warm wood work zone around a well-made signal bench. Up close the bench is the best model in the room. The green filter board has copper traces and jacks, the slot pads are clear, the tilted scope cabinet has a live canvas screen, and the candy-style resistor/coil/capacitor cans, rod rack, antenna ground-plane disc, lever and round LOG button all read at bench view and give far more than 6 cues. Outlines and the toon ramp are consistent, and every lit surface is toon() (366 toon, 119 basic, no Standard/Phong). The weak models are the room fixtures and clutter. The dome is a walk-through, un-faded half-shell with a blank 20 m² exterior and a telescope poking through it. The rack is a plain navy box with a floating one-sided plaque and no cable to the bench. The motor looks like a cable reel and is carried overhead, with an offset bug. Two exhibits (dish, prism) read as a bowl and a flag. The gallery light rail floats when the back wall cuts away. The clutter repeats: 13 blob-hued beanbags, 10 identical unlit lamps, purple shelves of saturated block books, and job-yellow crates.
notes.clarity: Job-yellow (#ffc94d/#ffd66b) sits on a beanbag, a chair and a dozen crates, while the motor cart (the first job item) is teal. At the start the most eye-catching yellow shapes are therefore decoration. The objective marker is a flat, semi-transparent yellow cone with no outline. From a high orbit it reads as a yellow leaf on the rug (shots 13-o90, 63b), and at the start it covers the ROOF RECEIVER plaque. The receiver line isn't drawn from the rack to the bench, so 'away from the receiver' and 'past the motor' have no visible anchor in the room. The safety sentence on the back wall is hidden behind the plinths and a clutter desk. Gallery panel names read at zoom 9, but the λ/f lines are about 8–10 px and unreadable at the game camera (fine as decoration, not as teaching).
notes.playability: Pip can walk through the dome shell and then vanishes completely behind it from the back orbit (shots 66b, 72), the main playability issue from this dimension. The cart carry lifts the cart to head height, and it lands tilted on furniture. The tall bookshelf tips over when Pip brushes it (shot 30), which is fine as chaos. Draw calls are 1084 (60 fps on the host GPU). The browser closed with no console or page errors on every script (g.close() returned []).
notes.fun: The win push-in frames the bench and gallery but not the dome, so the one celebratory change (the stars brighten) happens off screen, and Pip is clipped at the left edge. Confetti and the result card work. The room offers little physical comedy beyond knocking over lamps and shelves.
notes.teaching: From the model side, the rack, the motor and the bench cable need to be one visible physical system (rack jack → floor lead → bench RECEIVER) for the EMI and rerouting lesson to land. The motor needs motor cues (fins, shaft, terminal box, visible noise arcs) rather than a reel silhouette. The exhibits should physically depict what they label: a dish with a feed horn, and a prism splitting a white beam.
